Data.title: Crypto Analyst Shares Long Term XRP and XLM Price Targets
Data.body: Digital asset prices have long divided opinion between speculators and those who see a structural shift coming. Crypto enthusiast Mino sits firmly in the second camp. In a recent tweet , Mino laid out a set of long-term price targets that place several major digital assets well beyond their current valuations. Mino’s targets include XRP at $1,000–$10,000, QNT at $50,000, XLM at $1,000, XDC at $10,000, IOTA at $50–$100, ALGO at $10–$20, ONDO at $100, and HBAR at $10. My long-term targets: $XRP $1,000–$10,000 $QNT $50,000 $XLM $1,000 $XDC $10,000 $IOTA $50–$100 $ALGO $10–$20 $ONDO $100 $HBAR $10 These prices look impossible because crypto is still being priced like speculation. If digital assets become financial infrastructure, today’s… pic.twitter.com/VwwfffLS0I — Mino (@Ripple_Mino) October 20, 2026 The Reasoning Behind the Numbers Mino did not present these figures as near-term predictions. He offered a clear rationale. “These prices look impossible because crypto is still being priced like speculation,” he wrote. “If digital assets become financial infrastructure, today’s impossible prices will not look impossible forever.” The argument rests on a single premise. If the market reprices digital assets as infrastructure rather than speculation, the valuation floor shifts entirely. Mino believes that shift is coming. XRP’s $1,000 Target Draws Wider Support Mino is not alone in targeting four-figure XRP. Dom Kwok, co-founder of EasyA, has made the $1,000 XRP call a consistent part of his public commentary. In a recent tweet that drew hundreds of thousands of views and hundreds of replies, Kwok wrote, “$1,000 is more likely than ever.” He did not name XRP explicitly, but his long-standing public position leaves little room for ambiguity. Kwok has also put his conviction to a practical test. He calculated what a $1,000 investment in XRP would return at his target price. At the time of his post, $1,000 purchased approximately 735 XRP. At a $1,000 per token valuation, that holding becomes $735,000. Kwok called it “life-changing money.” Separately, Kwok ran a $1,000 XRP giveaway, asking followers to like and retweet to enter. The promotion generated significant engagement across the XRP community. Infrastructure or Speculation The core question in Mino’s post is not whether these prices are high. It is whether the market’s current pricing model is the right one. He argues it is not. Speculation drives today’s valuations. Infrastructure would drive tomorrow’s. That distinction matters for every asset on his list, but XRP carries the most immediate relevance given Ripple’s ongoing work in cross-border payments and the growing regulatory clarity around the token in the United States. Whether Mino’s targets prove accurate depends entirely on which version of the future arrives first. Disclaimer : This content is meant to inform and should not be considered financial advice. Data.title: Cambodia freezes $1B in Prince Group assets as countries split Chen Zhi's empire
Data.body: Cambodia has joined the international squeeze on assets tied to the Prince Group after courts authorized the country to freeze nearly $1 billion worth of assets, extending a streak of cross-border crackdowns that started after the group’s founder, Chen Zhi, was extradited to China. It is important to note that freezes are confiscations. The head of the secretariat of Cambodia’s Commission for Combating Technology-enabled Scams, Senior Minister Chhay Sinarith, speaking about the provisional nature of the orders, said the decision on whether the country gets to keep the frozen assets is up to judges, per reporting by The Phnom Penh Post. What did Cambodia freeze from Prince Group? According to Sinarith, the $1 billion in assets that Cambodia froze from Prince Group includes more than $300 million in cash across multiple bank accounts, as well as buildings, casinos, real estate parcels, and movable property. Cambodia has been hot on Chen Zhi’s trail since December 2025, when the Cambodian citizenship Chen earned in 2014 was revoked via a royal decree. By January 6, he was arrested by Cambodian police and extradited to China. Two days later, the National Bank of Cambodia ordered the Chen-founded lender, Prince Bank, into liquidation. Investigators have attributed roughly 198 companies to Chen’s Prince Group , with 98 inside Cambodia and 100 overseas. That sequence of events marked a sharp turn in fortunes for Chen, who at one point advised two generations of Cambodian leaders, Prime Minister Hun Manet and his father, Hun Sen. Other Prince Group members are also in custody Chen Zhi is not the only top-level Prince Group executive to have been arrested or arraigned in court. Others include Li Song, Liu Yin, Eang Soklim, Eng Dara and Huang Ron. There are court warrants out for 32 accused people in total, with four others under judicial supervision and five more suspects still being identified. Eng Dara, a 45-year-old Cambodian businessman and former director of Jin Bei Group, drew sanctions from both the UK and US in 2025 over suspected involvement in scam centers accused of forced labor. Eang Soklim was named as the figurehead of a scam compound in Prey Veng province. Cambodia is seeking INTERPOL Red Notices for another 29 people suspected to have fled the country. It is also sharing intelligence with the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and China’s Ministry of Public Security. The US Bitcoin case is still unfinished Washington is in a comparable holding pattern. The US Justice Department seized roughly 127,271 Bitcoin in October 2025, valued at $15 billion then and around $9 billion by March 2026, in what it called its largest forfeiture ever. Blockchain firm Elliptic traced the coins to LuBian, a mining operation with ties to China and Iran. The Bitcoin remains in government custody, and the forfeiture has not been finalized. The ICIJ reported that the Justice Department has rejected claims filed by lawyers for hundreds of alleged scam victims. Other jurisdictions have piled on. Hong Kong’s High Court froze about $1.1 billion in Chen’s deposits, properties and shares, Cryptopolitan reported , and Britain has frozen London mansions tied to alleged Prince Group associate Hu Xiaowei. Chen faces fraud and illegal gambling charges in China and up to 40 years if convicted of US wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy. Prince Group has denied wrongdoing. Data.title: 5 Reasons 67K+ Businesses Choose CCPayment for Crypto Payments Subheading: From accepting digital assets to putting funds to work, CCPayment addresses five prac...
Data.body: A customer pays in crypto and gets on with their day. For the business, the money still has work to do. An order needs reconciling, a partner’s commission is due and a supplier expects dollars in a bank account. The checkout is where those obligations begin. It is also where the business case for crypto payments faces its first real test. More ways to pay can help win a sale. What happens afterwards determines how easily that revenue can be accounted for, distributed and spent. Stablecoins bring the issue into focus: receiving digital dollars is useful, but those funds must also fit the routines of a working finance team. CCPayment crypto payment solutions are built around that need. The B2B crypto payment gateway, chosen by more than 67,000 businesses according to the company, connects incoming payments, payouts and settlement with existing systems and controls. Behind the adoption figure are five practical reasons for businesses to consider. 1. Customers can pay in crypto without creating a separate business process A customer wants to pay with digital assets. The business wants to complete the sale and know which order has been paid. When those needs are handled separately, staff can end up checking transfers manually and matching wallet activity to customer records. CCPayment supports crypto and stablecoin pay-ins: incoming payments from customers or counterparties. Businesses can accept cryptocurrency payments as part of their commercial operations, giving customers an additional payment option while building a process around how funds are received. For an online merchant, the value is straightforward: supporting a customer's payment preference without treating each crypto purchase as a special case. Implementation still needs to account for supported assets, networks and payment confirmation requirements, alongside availability in the relevant jurisdiction. 2. Paying more people should not mean repeating more work A business making occasional payments can tolerate some manual administration. A platform paying merchants, traders, partners or affiliates faces a different challenge: the same tasks multiply with every recipient. CCPayment’s Batch Payout API allows businesses to organize up to 500 crypto payouts under one master order. Teams can validate recipient addresses and Memos before sending, choose between faster batch execution and more controllable sequential execution, and track each recipient’s payment status, network fee and transaction ID separately. Consider an affiliate business managing commissions across multiple partners. Its operational challenge is getting approved amounts to the correct recipients and keeping records that finance can reconcile. Payout automation can support that process, provided the business maintains accurate recipient information, approval procedures and sufficient balances. The benefit is less repetitive handling. Responsibility for checking payment instructions and meeting applicable obligations remains with the business. 3. Crypto payments can fit the systems teams already use Adding a payment method becomes harder when it creates another disconnected source of information. If a cashier system, customer relationship management platform and finance team hold different versions of a transaction's status, someone has to resolve the gaps. CCPayment's crypto payment API provides a way to connect payment capabilities with existing systems. An API allows software applications to exchange information, helping businesses incorporate crypto activity into their cashier, CRM, finance and operational processes. For product teams, this creates a route to building payments around an established customer journey. For operations teams, a properly implemented connection can reduce the need to move information manually between systems. The CCPayment API documentation gives technical teams a starting point for assessing implementation. Integration still requires development, testing and decisions about transaction records, status updates and exception handling. 4. Payment controls belong inside the workflow Receiving funds is only part of running a payment operation. Businesses also need to understand transaction risk and decide when activity requires further review. Adding crypto should make those responsibilities part of the implementation discussion from the outset. CCPayment includes KYT and AML controls within its compliance-oriented workflows. KYT, or Know Your Transaction, involves examining transaction activity for potential risk. AML means anti-money laundering: the controls and procedures used to help detect and prevent illicit financial activity. These capabilities support a more disciplined approach to B2B crypto payments by making risk monitoring part of the operational picture. They do not replace a business's own compliance responsibilities. Teams still need appropriate governance, escalation procedures and reconciliation, with requirements depending on their activities and jurisdictions. The practical value is support for those processes as payment operations develop. 5. Receiving stablecoins is more useful when settlement is connected A business may collect digital assets while paying suppliers and operating expenses in traditional currency. That creates a treasury question: how does revenue move from a crypto balance into funds the business can use through its banking arrangements? CCPayment brings collection, payout workflows and settlement options into one infrastructure layer. Its USDT-to-USD settlement for eligible businesses supports conversion and settlement via SWIFT, connecting stablecoin balances with traditional banking workflows. For eligible businesses, this provides a route between accepting USDT and receiving USD through a supported bank account. Settlement remains subject to eligibility, required checks, banking availability and applicable local requirements; processing times and costs also matter when planning cash flow. The wider benefit is continuity across the payment journey, with collection and settlement considered together. Making crypto work for the business CCPayment's adoption milestone gives the story scale. Its product proposition gives businesses something concrete to assess: how incoming payments, outgoing transfers, integration, controls and settlement fit their operations. Successful adoption still depends on sound implementation and an understanding of digital asset and operational risks. For businesses evaluating crypto payments, the useful starting point is identifying where the current process creates work, then assessing how CCPayment can help. Data.title: CoinCDX denies hack as researchers trace outflows to former hot wallets
Data.body: On-chain data showed suspicious transactions from a wallet linked to the CoinCDX exchange. Over $15M in stablecoins were moved from the wallet, which was exposed in an earlier breach in 2025. The Indian crypto exchange CoinCDX is in the midst of a theft investigation. On-chain data linked a sudden outflow of funds from a wallet previously known to belong to the exchange. The exchange denies that the wallet is currently under its control, claiming it was falsely flagged on Arkham Intelligence. ‘ The addresses tagged by Arkham used to belong to CoinDCX before the last year hack ie July 2025. These addresses were generated in Jan 2025 and were compromised in the previous hack in July 2025. The hackers seem to be re-using the old wallet addresses and this sounds like a false alarm, ’ explained on X the exchange’s co-founder Sumit Gupta. The wallet transfers were noted late on October 21, moving $15.99M in USDT and 5,783.81 TRX. The funds were sent to an intermediary address , which was then emptied out, with some of the USDT reaching Binance hot wallets, as well as OKX and Gate. CoinCDX wallet was still used in DeFi protocols While CoinCDX denied using the wallet or controlling it, the address was still found to be active long after the 2025 exploit. On-chain researcher ZachXBT noted the wallet has still been used as a liquidity provider , while also sweeping user deposits. Additionally, ZachXBT noted CoinCDX still has to account for around $15.8M in user funds not accounted for in a transparent proof of reserves. As Cryptopolitan previously reported , CoinCDX has been flagged as an exchange used in fraud laundering. In 2025, the exchange also suffered a hack taking up to $44M. The recent movement of funds may not represent another wallet theft, but actually show CoinCDX users still deposited to the wallet for at least 10 months after the 2025 hack. ZachXBT also discovered the current hot wallets still sent gas to the compromised address as late as April 2026. CoinCDX is a relatively small exchange, with $1.15M in daily volume for the past 24 hours. The exchange’s most active pair is between fiat and USDT, with a limited number of assets offered. The exchange is seen as inherently risky, but now there are more doubts that the market operator may have failed to protect user funds, allowing deposits to refill an already compromised wallet. Can the CoinCDX funds be salvaged? In an unusual move, the funds from CoinCDX were moved to centralized exchanges. Most of the funds were also in USDT, meaning either Tether or the exchanges can freeze and revert the loss, but that depends on CoinCDX confirming the exploit. The fund movements from the exploiter wallet also repeated the previous CoinCDX hack, where the funds were laundered through centralized markets. Currently, CoinCDX is suspected of flawed security practices and of actually reusing its compromised wallets , while not giving sufficient proof of the safety of user funds. CoinCDX once again issued a statement that it did not interact with those wallets, going against the on-chain evidence. The CoinCDX exposure is a relatively rare event, as most of the hacks are targeting decentralized protocols. The suspected exploit against CoinCDX arrives at a time when crypto users are becoming more wary of hacks and accidental exposure, including the compromised private keys through Railway and the potential effects of the newly discovered PHP vulnerabilities . The CoinCDX exploit is still not fully understood, but if the exchange diverted user funds to a compromised address, it would further undermine trust in depositing crypto to exchange wallets. On-chain research found additional links between the hacker’s wallets and addresses used by CoinCDX, as noted by @DarcyAri, the account that first noticed the suspicious transfers. Data.title: BTC, HYPE, and ZEC Ready for a Rebound? Analyst Explains Why
Data.body: The cryptocurrency market enjoyed a short-lived rebound before sellers regained control over the past several hours. Some leading digital assets, including Bitcoin (BTC), Hyperliquid (HYPE), and Zcash (ZEC), were not spared in the latest pullback, all of which entered red territory. However, key indicators suggest they might soon recover the losses and head north. BTC to Bounce Back? Just hours ago, the primary cryptocurrency looked ready to reclaim $85,000, but it was rejected and now trades near $81,700 (per CoinGecko). Analyst Ali Martinez noted that as it approached $85K, the TD Sequential flashed a sell signal, foreshadowing the correction that followed. He said the same indicator has now printed a buy signal, suggesting the pullback may be nearing its end and potentially setting the stage for a recovery. Other popular market observers who commented on BTC’s recent performance include Wealthmanager and Joep Gerla. The former said the price is heading toward rising support around $81,500, and if buyers defend it, $83,500 and $85,000 come back into play. Joep Gerla noted that BTC got rejected near $85,000 at the top of the volume profile, adding that the structure stays bullish as long as the price remains above $80,000. “Lose $80K, and it weakens,” he warned. Renewed institutional demand supports the bullish view. After a period of heavy outflows, spot BTC ETFs posted three green days in a row, suggesting pension funds, hedge funds, and other conservative investors are once again increasing their exposure to the asset. In fact, the inflows in the past 24 hours reached nearly $530 million, the highest figure in the last month. Spot BTC ETFs, Source: SoSoValue HYPE and ZEC Hyperliquid’s native token jumped to almost $82 yesterday (October 21), but is currently worth just under $78. Martinez said a TD Sequential sell signal appeared around its local top, and the same indicator has now flipped bullish. “If $78 holds, HYPE could rebound toward $82 or higher,” he predicted. The privacy coin ZEC also rallied substantially and briefly surged above $1,360. Martinez explained that, as with BTC and HYPE, a TD Sequential sell signal acted as an early warning of the pullback that later dragged the asset to its current value of around $1,240. “With a buy signal now flashing, I’m watching the $1,250 support. If it holds, ZEC could rebound toward $1,350,” the analyst concluded. The post BTC, HYPE, and ZEC Ready for a Rebound? Analyst Explains Why appeared first on CryptoPotato .

Data.title: China’s Decision Affects Bitcoin, XRP, and Three Altcoins! Legal Battle Continues for Billions of Dollars Worth of Assets!
Data.body: According to Coindesk, China, known for its bans on Bitcoin and cryptocurrencies, is targeting the confiscation of 61,896 Bitcoins worth billions of dollars, linked to a fundraising scam that cost investors approximately 20 billion yuan. A court in Tianjin has granted a request to seize Bitcoin and other assets linked to Qian Zhimin. Six-Month Application Process in China! The Tianjin Court announced that it has accepted the prosecutor’s confiscation request, and the confiscation order covers Bitcoins as well as other cryptocurrencies, cash, jewelry, and financial assets. The court has opened a six-month application period for victims and other interested parties to join the case. Victims who do not participate in the process also have the option of claiming compensation from the recovered assets. As you may recall, the UK High Court recently ruled that claims involving more than 61,000 Bitcoins should be evaluated according to Chinese law. XRP, Dogecoin, and Other Assets Also Subject to Confiscation! The confiscation request includes more than just Bitcoin. Other assets listed by the court reportedly include XRP. “Approximately 72,745 Bitcoin Cash Approximately 72,745 Bitcoin Gold Approximately 72,745 Bitcoin SV More than 3.6 million XRP More than 70 million Dogecoin” The file reportedly includes cash in various currencies, jewelry, bank accounts, and various financial investments. British authorities have seized assets linked to the investigation, and it is reported that some crypto assets have been converted into other forms of assets. Chinese prosecutors are also seeking the recovery of these assets and, where appropriate, the return of money owed to victims. *This is not investment advice. Data.title: Market Brief: Can Bitcoin Reach $100K Before Year-End?
Data.body: Summary Analysts remain divided on whether Bitcoin can reach $100,000 before year-end. Over the past two weeks, institutional demand has shown early signs of recovery. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded their largest daily net inflow in a month on October 19, as recent outflow pressure began to ease. Sustained ETF inflows, alongside easing inflation and reduced expectations for further Fed rate hikes, would provide stronger support for Bitcoin’s recovery toward $100K. Originally published on October 21, 2026 Bitcoin is trading around $83K, needing a gain of more than 20% to reach the $100K milestone. While Bitwise expects BTC to reclaim six figures before year-end, other analysts remain cautious as inflation and interest rate uncertainty continue to weigh on the market. Meanwhile, Bitcoin’s volatility has narrowed considerably, ETF flows are showing early signs of recovery, and JPMorgan has introduced its first long-term return forecast for Bitcoin. With just over two months left in 2026, what could push BTC back toward $100K? Analysts remain divided on whether Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) can reach $100,000 before year-end. Bitwise Head of Research Ryan Rasmussen is optimistic, expecting Bitcoin to finish 2026 above $100K, supported by growing institutional adoption, continued ETF demand, and improving regulatory clarity. In contrast, LO:TECH Head of Research Adam Morgan McCarthy expects BTC to end the year between $85K and $95K, citing persistent inflation and the possibility of further Fed rate hikes. The difference largely comes down to whether institutional demand can overcome tighter monetary conditions. September U.S. CPI rose 3.7% year-over-year, its highest reading since January, driven largely by higher energy prices. Persistent inflation could keep the Fed from easing monetary conditions and limit the liquidity available to risk assets. Over the past two weeks, institutional demand has shown early signs of recovery. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded their largest daily net inflow in a month on October 19, as recent outflow pressure began to ease. Sustained ETF inflows, alongside easing inflation and reduced expectations for further Fed rate hikes, would provide stronger support for Bitcoin’s recovery toward $100K. Is Bitcoin Preparing for a Big Move? Bitcoin’s daily Bollinger Bands have narrowed to one of their tightest levels in the past two and a half years. Similar periods of volatility compression have sometimes preceded sharp price moves, making the current consolidation worth watching. However, low volatility offers little guidance on the direction of the next move. A breakout above the upper Bollinger Band, supported by rising trading volume and stronger spot demand, would suggest improving bullish momentum. Conversely, renewed macroeconomic pressure or weakening demand could trigger another downward move. JPMorgan Forecasts 10% Annual BTC Returns In its 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, JPMorgan Asset Management introduced its first long-term return forecast for Bitcoin, projecting a 10% compounded annual return over the coming decade. That exceeds its forecasts for U.S. large-cap equities at 7.5% and gold at 5.5%, placing Bitcoin among the highest return assets in its long-term projections. However, the expected returns come with considerably greater risk. JPMorgan estimates Bitcoin’s annualized volatility at 55%, compared with 18% for U.S. large-cap equities and 17.2% for gold. Its unstable correlations with traditional assets also remain a challenge for portfolio diversification. JPMorgan’s first formal long-term Bitcoin forecast marks a meaningful step in institutional research. Major asset managers are increasingly evaluating Bitcoin alongside traditional assets, although its high volatility continues to limit broader portfolio adoption. What Would It Take to Reach $100K? Bitcoin needs to gain more than 20% from its current level to reach $100K before the end of 2026. 3 developments would strengthen the case for a year-end recovery: Easing macro pressure: Lower inflation and reduced expectations for further Fed rate hikes could improve liquidity conditions. Sustained institutional demand: Continued ETF inflows would help confirm that the recent improvement in buying activity is gaining momentum. A confirmed technical breakout: Rising trading volume and stronger spot demand would provide more convincing evidence of upward momentum. Bitcoin’s longer-term institutional outlook is becoming more constructive, but its near-term direction remains sensitive to inflation, monetary policy, and capital flows.
